title: P2 FIRST RUN: exact finite-support bounds on the risk difference of two fixed models under an unknown missingness policy
work_id_mapping: none (P2 is not mapped to any pre-existing Work ID; the repository had no prior work)

preregistration.disclosure: A smoke test on this exact scenario (same joint, models, q) was executed before this config was committed; it printed Delta(q), intervals for Gamma in {1,5/4,2,4,inf} and a Gamma* bracket for the pattern set. No scenario parameter was changed after that smoke test. Environments, Gamma grid, sampling design and hypotheses were written after it.

hypotheses.H-ENG: Every LP returns an exact certificate (primal-dual gap 0 or Farkas); Gamma=1 gives the point Delta(q); intervals are nested in Gamma and in constraint strength; pi* in Pi implies Delta(pi*) in interval; support violations are flagged / reported INFEASIBLE rather than as numbers.
hypotheses.H1: Pattern-marginal set, primary scenario: the ranking-transfer threshold Gamma* is finite and the closed-form certified value Gamma_cf satisfies Gamma_cf <= Gamma*.
hypotheses.H2: At Gamma_pre = 2 the joint interval (same unknown policy for both models) is strictly narrower than the separate-bounds interval, for every constraint kind.
hypotheses.H3: Prop. 2 prediction: under Brier loss with non-constant f_A - f_B, the joint interval has positive width for every Gamma > 1 and every constraint kind including the unlabelled observed law; controls with additively separable D (C1) or constant f_A - f_B (C2, observed-law only) have zero width.
hypotheses.H4: Plug-in intervals (empirical complete-data joint) do not reliably contain the population interval; containment frequency is reported per n with a Wilson interval, no nominal level is claimed.

preregistration.primary_metric: Gamma* bracket (pattern-marginal set) for the primary scenario, compared with Gamma_cf.
secondary_metrics: interval endpoints and widths per (Gamma, kind)

independent_unit.population_parts: one hand-specified finite population (n_units = 1): no statistical generalisation across scenarios is possible; environments are hand-specified illustrations, not samples.
independent_unit.sampling_part: independent replication (fresh i.i.d. complete-data sample of size n per replication)

stop_conditions: Any LP without a valid exact certificate -> stop, report FAIL, do not use its numbers.
Any case with pi* in Pi but Delta(pi*) outside the interval -> stop (bug).
Wall time over 120 s -> abort; unfinished parts are NOT_RUN.
Scientific: if the only supported statement is 'MNAR can reverse random-dropout rankings', make no method claim.

model_A.note: idealised random-dropout-trained model: P(Y=1 | X_r = x_r)

model_B.note: fill missing features with the population mode, then full-data P(Y=1 | X)

support_violation.deployment: independent dropout with the primary drop rates (uses mask 00, which q_evaluator never produces)

controls.C1_additive_D: replace D by its ANOVA additive part D - D_int (w, q weights)

C2_constant_shift_B.note: B' = A + kappa, so f_A - f_B' is constant
